title: (CommunityCloud) Moving slider seems to generate 2 new (empty) window.history states
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

While investigating https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-9184 I noticed my browser history (i.e. back navigation) got _filled_ with `window.history` state entries that don't actually seem to do anything when you navigate backwards or forwards through them. It seems like this only affects community cloud? I was unable to reproduce on a local instance of streamlit.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
st.slider("Slider (1.0 float step)", min_value=1.50, max_value=100.50, value=(2.5, 41.5), step=1.0)
st.slider("Slider (1.1 float step)", min_value=1.50, max_value=100.50, value=(2.5, 41.5), step=1.1)
st.slider("Slider (int step)", min_value=1, max_value=100, value=(2, 40), step=3)
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Go to https://issues.streamlit.app/?issue=gh-9184 in MS Edge or Opera One(version: 114.0.5282.185) -- it probably works in Chrome too but I didn't have that installed to test.
2. Right click on the browser "Back" button to see the tab history. It should look something like this
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6154ef06-c882-4c98-ad93-b340fb92a935)
3. Adjust the sliders on the page a couple of times.
4. Go back and right-click on the browser "Back" button. 
![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9de642ae-90eb-4783-b46f-0708295f6032)

5. Clicking the "Back" button doesn't actually change any kind of state on the page (e.g. it doesn't move the sliders back to their old positions -- not that I was really expecting it to do that)



### Expected Behavior

We shouldn't be putting do-nothing states into user's `window.history` on widget interaction.

### Current Behavior

![image](https://external-content.duckduckgo.com/iu/?u=https%3A%2F%2Fi.imgflip.com%2F1rpt5c.jpg&f=1&nofb=1&ipt=53ccae2a973a336828bfcaf6c76821c6c0278814b51b2fd6bdaca1150f84b1ce&ipo=images)

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: whatever you guys were running on Community Cloud in Nov 2024
- Python version: _probably_ 3.10, based on what I know about community cloud
- Operating System: Windows
- Browser: Tested on MS Edge Version 131.0.2903.51 and Opera One (version: 114.0.5282.185)


### Additional Information
